title: Colosseum
blurb: The Flavian Amphitheatre in Rome as it stands today: the south outer wall collapsed in the 1349 earthquake, the velarium and wooden gallery are gone, and the arena floor is gone, leaving Domitian's hypogeum exposed. Explore 104 components across 10 systems: the surviving north arcade bays, the exposed hypogeum machinery, and the 19th century brick shoring.

systems.name: Outer Facade Arcades
systems.description: Eighty travertine bays in three superimposed orders, Doric below, Ionic in the middle, Corinthian above, grouped ten ways per tier.

systems.name: Attic and Crown
systems.description: The solid attic story with Corinthian pilasters and windows, the crowning cornice, and the 240 mast corbels of the velarium.

systems.name: Main Entrances
systems.description: Four unnumbered axial entrances, 76 numbered spectator entrances, and the imperial passage to the pulvinar.

systems.name: Seating Cavea
systems.description: Tiered marble seating for about 50,000 spectators, strictly ordered by class, from the senators podium to the wooden top gallery.

systems.name: Circulation
systems.description: Annular corridors, vomitoria, and stairs that filled and emptied the building in a few minutes.

systems.name: Support Structure
systems.description: Radial and annular walls, inner wall rings, and the travertine pressure skeleton carrying the cavea.

systems.name: Arena
systems.description: The wooden sand covered floor, its 5 m surrounding wall, the protective fence, and the marble passage.

systems.name: Hypogeum
systems.description: The subterranean two level network of corridors, chambers, animal dens, and lifting machinery beneath the arena.

systems.name: Ruin and Restoration
systems.description: The current state: the south outer wall collapsed in the 1349 earthquake, and the 1807 and 1827 brick shoring wedges brace the broken ends of the surviving north arcades.

systems.name: Materials
systems.description: Representative samples of the building materials: travertine, brick faced concrete, tuff, marble, and iron clamps.

explanations.ne attic window panels: NE attic window panels: small rectangular windows pierce the 2.10 m attic band over every second arch, with a second row cut between every second pair of pilasters above. Window positions are schematic.

explanations.bronze shields (clipea): Bronze shields (clipea) fixed in the spaces between the attic pilasters, directly beneath the uppermost cornice. Their exact positions are schematic.
explanations.entablature and cornice: Entablatures of 2.35 m and 2.10 m and attic bands of 1.95 m and 2.10 m separate the tiers; the crowning cornice carried the mast sockets of the velarium.
explanations.ne velarium mast corbels (60): NE velarium mast corbels: sixty of the 240 stone corbels ringed around the top of the attic, three socketed consoles between each pair of pilasters, carrying the masts of the retractable velarium.
explanations.nw velarium mast corbels (60): NW velarium mast corbels: sixty of the 240 stone corbels ringed around the top of the attic, three socketed consoles between each pair of pilasters, carrying the masts of the retractable velarium.
explanations.stylobate base ring: The outer wall stands on a raised two step travertine stylobate.
explanations.travertine pavement and cippi: A 17.50 m wide travertine pavement surrounds the building; five stone cippi posts still stand on the east side, 18 m out from the perimeter.
explanations.north axial entrance portal: The northern axial entrance was reserved for the Roman Emperor and his aides. Its arches were wider and more highly ornamented than the rest, and a wide passage led from it directly to the imperial box (pulvinar) on the podium.
explanations.north entrance arch: The decorated arch framing the northern imperial entrance. All four axial entrances were richly decorated with painted stucco reliefs, of which fragments survive.
explanations.east axial entrance: The major axis entrances led directly into the arena, admitting processions and equipment.
explanations.west axial entrance: The western major axis entrance led directly into the arena.
explanations.ne numbered entrances (19): NE numbered entrances: nineteen of the 76 numbered ground floor entrances for ordinary spectators. Entrances XXIII to LIIII still survive on the north side. Door panels are schematic.
explanations.nw numbered entrances (19): NW numbered entrances: nineteen of the 76 numbered ground floor entrances for ordinary spectators. Entrances XXIII to LIIII still survive on the north side. Door panels are schematic.
explanations.imperial passage to the pulvinar: A wide passage led from the northern imperial entrance directly to the imperial box (pulvinar) on the podium. Its routing is schematic.
explanations.porta triumphalis (east arena gate): The Porta Triumphalis, the eastern gate of the arena at the end of the major axis, through which gladiators and wild animals entered and by which victorious combatants departed.
explanations.porta libitinensis (west arena gate): The Porta Libitinensis, the western gate of the arena, through which the mortally wounded and the dead were carried out.
explanations.podium ring: Senators sat on a marble podium raised about 4 m above the arena, fronted by a bronze balustrade.
explanations.podium bronze balustrade: A bronze balustrade fronted the senators marble podium above the arena. Its form is schematic.

explanations.imperial box (pulvinar): The pulvinar, the imperial box, on the podium at the north end of the minor axis, reached by a wide passage from the northern entrance.
explanations.box of the praefectus urbi: The prefect of the city had his own box on the podium, opposite the imperial box.
explanations.praecinctiones and baltei: Horizontal walkways (praecinctiones) and low parapet walls (baltei) divided the seating tiers by social class.
explanations.ground floor outer ambulatory: The outer of two lofty arched corridors encircling the building at ground level between the outer wall and the third wall.
explanations.ground floor inner ambulatory: The inner of the two ground floor annular corridors serving the seating.
explanations.second floor outer corridor: The outer annular corridor of the second story, distributing spectators to the middle seating tiers.
explanations.second floor inner corridor: The inner corridor of the second story, divided into an upper and a lower section, with ingeniously arranged flights of steps leading to the topmost story.
explanations.third floor outer corridor: The outer annular corridor of the third story, serving the upper seats and the wooden gallery.
explanations.third floor inner corridor: The inner corridor of the third story, with ingeniously arranged flights of steps leading to the topmost story and the upper part of the second tier of seats.
explanations.grand staircase, north: A monumental stair near the northern axial entrance, connecting the ground floor ambulatory with the upper corridors. Its exact form and routing are schematic.
explanations.lower vomitoria mouths (16): Sixteen vomitoria mouths at the junction between the maenianum primum and the maenianum secundum. Stair passages arranged in fours could disgorge the crowd in only a few minutes. Positions are schematic.
explanations.upper vomitoria mouths (16): Sixteen vomitoria mouths at the junction between the maenianum secundum and the wooden gallery. Stair passages arranged in fours could disgorge the crowd in only a few minutes. Positions are schematic.
explanations.ne radial stair flights (4): NE radial stair flights: four flights climbing the cavea slope between the wedge shaped seating sections. Positions are schematic.
explanations.nw radial stair flights (4): NW radial stair flights: four flights climbing the cavea slope between the wedge shaped seating sections. Positions are schematic.
explanations.ne radial support walls (20): NE radial support walls: twenty of the eighty radiating walls that matched the lower arcade piers in number and carried the sloping cavea floor with its marble seats.
explanations.nw radial support walls (20): NW radial support walls: twenty of the eighty radiating walls that matched the lower arcade piers in number and carried the sloping cavea floor with its marble seats.
explanations.inner annular support wall: The inner of the concentric annular walls tying the radial walls together beneath the seating slope. Its exact radius is schematic.
explanations.outer annular support wall: The outer of the concentric annular walls tying the radial walls together beneath the seating slope. Its exact radius is schematic.
explanations.second inner wall: The second inner wall stands 5.80 m inside the outer wall.
explanations.third inner wall: The third inner wall stands 4.50 m inside the second.
explanations.northeast travertine pressure skeleton: Northeast half of Vespasian's inner travertine skeleton, which carried the greatest structural loads and rose no higher than the second story. The southern half is gone with the collapsed outer wall. Column positions are schematic.
explanations.northwest travertine pressure skeleton: Northwest half of Vespasian's inner travertine skeleton, which carried the greatest structural loads and rose no higher than the second story. The southern half is gone with the collapsed outer wall. Column positions are schematic.

explanations.sw arena wall section: The SW section of the 5 m high wall that ringed the arena, above which the seating rose.

explanations.west gladiator passage: West gladiator passage: the hypogeum held gladiators before contests, and tunnels linked it to points outside the building. Passage routing is schematic.

explanations.tunnel connecting ramps: Ramps connecting the two levels of the hypogeum tunnel network. Their exact routing is schematic.
explanations.ne vertical shafts (20): NE vertical shafts: twenty of the eighty shafts that gave caged animals and scenery instant access to the arena floor.
explanations.nw vertical shafts (20): NW vertical shafts: twenty of the eighty shafts that gave caged animals and scenery instant access to the arena floor.

explanations.elevator winch drums: Slave powered winch drums that worked the elevators and trapdoors of the hypogeum.
explanations.pulley rigging posts: Elevators and pulleys that raised and lowered scenery, props, and caged animals to the surface for release.
explanations.east hegmata platforms: East hinged hegmata platforms, which tilted up through trapdoors to deliver animals, scenery, and even elephants to the arena.
explanations.west hegmata platforms: West hinged hegmata platforms, which tilted up through trapdoors to deliver animals, scenery, and even elephants to the arena.
explanations.major axis subterranean passage: A subterranean passage on the line of the major axis, by which the hypogeum substructures were entered.
explanations.minor axis subterranean passage: A subterranean passage on the line of the minor axis, by which the hypogeum substructures were entered.
explanations.cryptoporticus of commodus: The cryptoporticus of Commodus was a vaulted underground passage linking the imperial areas to the arena.
explanations.hypogeum brick pavement: The hypogeum substructure walls stand 5.50 to 6.08 m high on a brick pavement, shown here beneath the tunnel network.
explanations.collapsed south wall, fallen blocks: Fallen travertine blocks from the outer south arcades, which collapsed in the earthquake of 1349 and lie where they fell on the pavement south of the building.
explanations.1807 brick shoring wedge: Triangular brick wedge added in 1807 to shore the broken eastern end of the surviving north arcades after the 1349 earthquake collapsed the south outer wall. Its position is schematic.
explanations.1827 brick shoring wedge: Triangular brick wedge added in 1827 to shore the broken western end of the surviving north arcades after the 1349 earthquake collapsed the south outer wall. Its position is schematic.
explanations.travertine block sample: The outer wall used over 100,000 cubic meters of travertine set without mortar, held by 300 tons of iron clamps. Representative sample shown.
explanations.brick faced concrete sample: Inner walls are concrete with and without brick facing. Representative sample shown.
explanations.tuff and sperone sample: Tuff and sperone, volcanic stones, were used in the lower parts of the inner walls. Representative sample shown.
explanations.marble seat sample: Marble faced the seats of the cavea and the podium. Representative sample shown.
explanations.iron clamp sample: The travertine blocks of the outer wall were set without mortar and locked with 300 tons of iron clamps. Representative sample shown.
